# 0x205 — `wheel_speeds`

DLC 8 · 100 Hz · status: **confirmed**

Front and rear wheel speed as two 16-bit words. The difference between them shows wheel slip under traction control and ABS.

## Layout

Bytes are numbered from 0. Multi-byte values are big-endian unless a row says otherwise. Bit 7 is the most significant bit of a byte.

| Byte | Content |
|---|---|
| B0 | `wheel_speed_front` |
| B1 | `wheel_speed_front` |
| B2 | `wheel_speed_rear` |
| B3 | `wheel_speed_rear` |
| B4 | — |
| B5 | `accel_level`, `b5_bit0_unknown` |
| B6 | `b6b7_always_zero` |
| B7 | `b6b7_always_zero` |

## Signals

| Signal | Where | Type | Value | Unit | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wheel_speed_front` | B0:B1 | uint16 BE | raw × 0.00990099 | km/h | confirmed (high) |
| `wheel_speed_rear` | B2:B3 | uint16 BE | raw × 0.00990099 | km/h | confirmed (medium) |
| `accel_level` | B5 bits 3..1 | 3-bit field | enum |  | hypothesis (medium) |
| `b5_bit0_unknown` | B5 bit 0 | flag | raw |  | unknown |
| `b6b7_always_zero` | B6:B7 | uint16 BE | raw |  | unknown |

### `wheel_speed_front`

Front wheel speed, raw / 101.0 = true km/h. The dash reads about 9 % higher than this, as most speedometers do. The dash trip meter counts 1.0388 × the distance integrated from this word, so a trip that matches the dash can be computed from the bus.

**Confirmed by:** Phone GPS speed on one ride; the dash speedometer on video on two others.

**How we know:** Compared with phone GPS Doppler speed over one ride: 181 steady pairs from 17 to 135 km/h give 100.8 raw per km/h, residual sd 0.4 km/h. The ratio falls slightly with speed (101.2 at 15-40 km/h, 100.4 above 120 km/h). Two earlier rides compared through video of the dash speedometer (linear from 11 to 170 km/h) agree with it. A cold-day ride (6-9 °C) gave raw / 101.0 = 0.997 × GPS again on three recordings (r 0.994-0.998). Trip meter: seven filmed steps of the dash trip over 10.4 km fit 1.0388 × the integrated front-wheel distance within ±1.2 m.

**Caveats:** The scale depends on tyre size, wear and pressure. GPS rides on one set of tyres.

**Example:** `0x205  2B 21 2B 78 00 04 00 00` → 109.3 km/h

### `wheel_speed_rear`

Rear wheel speed, same scale as the front. At steady speed it reads within 0.2 % of the front below 60 km/h and up to 1 % higher above 100 km/h.

**Confirmed by:** The front wheel word; the wheel-speed dip at rear ABS events.

**How we know:** Rear/front ratio over 2313 steady windows of one ride; when the rear wheel locks, the rear word drops 8-10 km/h below the front within a few frames and recovers.

**Example:** `0x205  2B 21 2B 78 00 04 00 00` → 110.2 km/h

### `accel_level`

A longitudinal acceleration level 0-7 with the bit order reversed: bit 3 is the least significant bit of the level and bit 1 the most significant, so level = bit3 + 2 × bit2 + 4 × bit1 (the value table maps the raw 3-bit field to the level). The level rises steadily with rear-wheel acceleration, about 0.11 g per step; level 0 covers any deceleration. B4 is always 0. Possibly a drive-force class used by the ABS unit for traction or lift control. An earlier reading of bit 3 as "ABS armed" does not fit.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | level 0 (decelerating) |
| 1 | level 4 |
| 2 | level 2 |
| 3 | level 6 |
| 4 | level 1 |
| 5 | level 5 |
| 6 | level 3 |
| 7 | level 7 |

**How we know:** Four full-rate rides of one day, moving, ordered by median rear-wheel acceleration: level 0 -0.10 g, 1 +0.02, 2 +0.12, 3 +0.24, 4 +0.36, 5 +0.47, 6 +0.56, 7 +0.66 g, with 41.7, 38.7, 12.0, 4.3, 2.0, 1.0, 0.3 and under 0.1 % of moving time. The reference is the wheel-speed derivative, not an independent sensor, hence hypothesis. Level 1 (bit 3 alone) is also what the frame shows at standstill.

**Example:** `0x205  2B 21 2B 78 00 04 00 00` → 2

### `b5_bit0_unknown`

Rarely set (under 0.1 % of frames). Not decoded.

### `b6b7_always_zero`

Always 0x0000 in every full-rate capture and long-ride log.

### Derived: `wheel_slip`

`wheel_speed_rear - wheel_speed_front` (km/h) — confirmed (high)

Positive when the rear wheel spins faster than the front (wheelspin on a loose surface), negative when the rear slows more than the front (rear lock-up).

**Confirmed by:** Rear ABS events; wheelspin on sand.

**How we know:** Negative by 8-10 km/h at each rear ABS event; positive by 4-9 km/h while the rear wheel spun on sand.
